# Plan employee training and development

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a role, promotion, control or business change creates a capability or training need. A role-based development plan with completed learning evidence and an assessment of practical capability.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Identify role and control-specific skill gaps

agent-runnable


Compare expected work with observed performance, new tools, customer commitments and required training. Separate mandatory certifications from optional development and record who needs each capability.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree learning objectives and support

human · human approval required


The employee and manager choose observable outcomes, learning time, mentoring and budget. Confirm any external qualification or training requirement with the relevant owner instead of assuming course attendance establishes competence.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Schedule learning and supervised practice

agent-runnable


Prepare a plan combining instruction, practice tasks, accessible materials and feedback. Assign the reviewer and keep production or customer work within the employee's current authorization.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Assess application of the new skill

human · human approval required


The employee performs an agreed practical task or assessment with appropriate supervision. Record the evidence and any gaps; completion of an automated quiz alone need not establish readiness for high-risk work.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Update the capability plan and review date

agent-runnable


Retain approved completion evidence, record role changes requiring access or authority review and agree the next development priorities. Revisit the plan when the job or control requirements change.

- Verify: A role-based development plan with completed learning evidence and an assessment of practical capability.
- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
